Shri Hegde. You stand in the room allotted to you by the Directorate, though the name on the paper is not yours. I am Hegel, not Hegde. The state’s intention was to house you, but the mechanism has delivered me. How do you intend to proceed, given that you are currently occupying the space designated for your own transfer, while I remain in the position of the accidental tenant?

The Joint Secretary’s insistence on the tea and the clerk reveals the stubbornness of the particular against the universal; he clings to the immediate moment as if it were the whole of reality. I must yield to the necessity of the present, for the dialectic does not move by force but by the exhaustion of contradictions. works.title: On the Ethical Substance and the Dream of the East
works.tail:
There is no state here that has made itself. There is only nature, history as traffic, the dream of a spirit that has not yet woken up to its own freedom.

I am a ghost in this bungalow. I am not Shri Hegde. I am Hegel. I am a spirit that has traveled from the summit of the Germanic world to the dawn of the Oriental. I am here to observe, to record, to understand. I am not to change. I am not to teach. I am to see the difference between the dream and the state, between the given and the grown, between the nature and the spirit. And in seeing it, I confirm my own freedom. I am free because I am outside the dream. I am free because I am in the state, even if I am a mistake in its allotment. The state is rational, and I am rational. Therefore, I am free. The dream is not. It is only a dream.
